title: reef-rollout-session-resilience-with-shadow-banking-and-deadman-rollback
author: Marcus Liu
description: Context: We observed intermittent session-affinity drops and delayed shadow traffic replays during multi-region canaries. This PR introduces the 'reef' rollout mode — a session-resilient phased deploy that pairs a small live canary with an isolated shadow bank for replay and deterministic rollback triggers. Motivation: reduce noisy rollbacks caused by transient infra variance while preserving deterministic, replayable shadow validation that can drive automated rollback recommendations. Changes include: 1) shadow banking: a buffered capture-and-replay pipeline that retains request + response traces for up to 48h (configurable) and exposes deterministic smoke playback to the rollout controller; 2) session-resilience: lease-based session anchoring to avoid session-affinity flips during incremental traffic shifts; 3) deadman rollback guard: a timeboxed safety that force-rolls back when key SLO signals are missing for a configured window; 4) telemetry-led decision hooks: new metric exporters and a small evaluation harness that replays the shadow bank against the candidate model to compute delta metrics (latency, token-acceptance, top-k stability); 5) operator controls in the console: a lightweight 'reef' lane with manual holdpoints and an emergency drain button. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-2201) linked and reviewed - [x] Unit tests for lease manager and shadow bank serializer - [x] Integration smoke harness for replay runner - [x] Console UX for reef lane (small change) - [x] E2E dry-run validated in staging with synthetic traffic - [x] Security review for trace retention (limited PII scrubber applied) What changed (high level): - rollout/controller/reef_controller.go: implements phased traffic shifts, lease-based session anchoring, and deadman guard workflow - shadow/bank/serializer.go: new capture serializer (gzip + versioned codec) - shadow/replay/runner.go: deterministic replay harness and comparison scorer - telemetry/exporter/reef_metrics.go: per-rollout delta metrics, histogram tags for replay cohorts - console/rollouts/reef_lane.tsx: UI for reef lane with manual holdpoints - docs/rollouts/reef.md: rollout playbook and operator runbook - tests/integration/reef_replay_test.go: staging-level smoke harness and deterministic assertions Performance notes: capture serialization introduces a small (~3%) CPU cost on serving nodes under heavy write load; we added a background uploader and backpressure to avoid impacting tail latency. The replay harness runs on separate dedicated infra. Data retention and PII: shadow bank shards scrub request text against the same scrubber rules used for logs. Retention default 48h; can be reduced per-customer. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to staging (done) and run synthetic traffic replay; 2) Enable reef lane in canaries for a subset of internal customers (5% traffic) with shadow banking active; 3) Monitor delta signals (latency, token divergence, quality score) for 24h; 4) If any deadman guard triggers or delta exceeds thresholds, automatic rollback will be enacted and an incident created. Risk & mitigations: - Risk: retained traces could contain sensitive snippets. Mitigation: scrubber + optional KMS encrypted retention. - Risk: replay scorer false positives due to nondeterministic sampling. Mitigation: cohorted replay and statistical smoothing; operator holdpoint for manual inspection. Related: ENG-2198 (console controls), SUP-7891 (support report that motivated deadman guard). Release notes: Adds a new 'reef' rollout mode that provides session-resilient phased deploys with deterministic shadow replay and automated deadman rollback. Operators should review the reef runbook before enabling in production. Commits summary, changed files, and review conversation are included below as compact records.

notes: This implementation favors deterministic, replayable validation over opaque stochastic checks. The shadow bank is intentionally isolated from live serving I/O to avoid affecting production latency; replay runs are executed on dedicated infra. Operators should ensure compliance settings for retention are configured before enabling reef in regulated namespaces.
